{{Short description|Stochastic process}}
{{Distinguish|Feller-continuous process}}

{{Refimprove|date=September 2009}}

In [[probability theory]] relating to [[stochastic processes]], a '''Feller process''' is a particular kind of [[Markov process]].

==Definitions==

Let <math display="inline">X</math> be a [[locally compact]] [[Hausdorff space]] with a [[countable set|countable]] [[base (topology)|base]]. Let <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> denote the space of all real-valued [[continuous function]]s on <math display="inline">X</math> that [[vanish at infinity]], equipped with the [[sup norms|sup-norm]] <math display="inline">\|f\|</math>. From analysis, we know that <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> with the sup norm is a [[Banach space]].

A '''Feller semigroup''' on <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> is a [[C0-semigroup#Contraction_semigroups|contraction C<sub>0</sub>-semigroup]] of [[Positive_linear_operator|positive  operators]] on <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math>.
Concretely, it is a collection <math display="inline">(T_t)_{t \ge 0}</math> of [[linear map]]s from <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> to itself with the following properties<ref>{{cite book |last1=Revuz |first1=Daniel |last2=Yor |first2=Marc |title=Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion |date=1999 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-06400-9}}</ref>:
* <math display="inline">T_t f \ge 0</math> for all <math display="inline">t \ge 0 </math> and <math display="inline">f \in C_0(X)</math> where <math display="inline">f \ge 0</math>, i.e., each <math display="inline">T_t</math> is a [[Positive_linear_operator|positive operator]];
* <math display="inline">\|T_t f\| \le \|f\|</math> for all <math display="inline">t \ge 0 </math> and <math display="inline">f \in C_0(X)</math>, i.e., it is a [[contraction mapping|contraction]] (in the weak sense);
* <math display="inline">T_0 = \operatorname{Id}</math> and <math display="inline">T_{t+s} = T_t \circ T_s</math> for all <math display="inline">s,t \ge 0</math>, i.e., it is a [[semigroup]];
* <math display="inline">\lim_{t \to 0} \|T_t f - f\| = 0</math> for every <math display="inline">f \in C_0(X)</math>. Using the semigroup property, this is equivalent to the map <math display="inline">T_t f</math> from <math display="inline">t \in [0,\infty)</math> to  <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> being [[right continuous]] for every <math display="inline">f</math>.

'''Warning''': This terminology is not uniform across the literature. In particular, the assumption that <math display="inline">T_t</math> maps <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> into itself
is replaced by some authors by the condition that it maps <math display="inline">C_b(X)</math>, the space of bounded continuous functions, into itself. 
The reason for this is twofold: first, it allows including processes that enter "from infinity" in finite time. Second, it is more suitable to the treatment of
spaces that are not locally compact and for which the notion of "vanishing at infinity" makes no sense.

A '''Feller transition function''' is a probability transition function associated with a Feller semigroup.

A '''Feller process''' is a [[Markov process]] with a Feller transition function.

== Generator ==

Feller processes (or transition semigroups) can be described by their [[infinitesimal generator (stochastic processes)|infinitesimal generator]]. A function <math display="inline">f</math> in <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> is said to be in the domain of the generator if the uniform limit

: <math> Af = \lim_{t\rightarrow 0} \frac{T_tf - f}{t},</math>

exists. The operator <math display="inline">A</math> is the generator of <math display="inline">(T_t)_{t \ge 0}</math>, and the space of functions on which it is defined is written as <math display="inline">D(A)</math>.

A characterization of operators that can occur as the infinitesimal generator of Feller processes is given by the [[Hille–Yosida theorem]]. This uses the resolvent of the Feller semigroup, defined below.

== Resolvent ==

The '''[[resolvent formalism|resolvent]]''' of a Feller process (or semigroup) is a collection of maps <math display="inline">(R_\lambda)_{\lambda > 0}</math> from <math display="inline">C_0(X)</math> to itself defined by
:<math>R_\lambda f = \int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}T_t f\,dt.</math>
It can be shown that it satisfies the identity
:<math>R_\lambda R_\mu = R_\mu R_\lambda = (R_\mu-R_\lambda)/(\lambda-\mu).</math>
Furthermore, for any fixed <math display="inline">\lambda > 0</math>, the image of <math display="inline">R_\lambda</math> is equal to the domain <math display="inline">D(A)</math> of the generator <math display="inline">A</math>, and
:<math>
\begin{align}
& R_\lambda = (\lambda - A)^{-1}, \\
& A = \lambda - R_\lambda^{-1}.
\end{align}
</math>

== Examples ==

* [[Brownian motion]] and the [[Poisson process]] are examples of Feller processes (with Feller semigroups given by <math display="inline">T_{t}f := \mathbb{E}[f(X_{t})]</math>). More generally, every [[Lévy process]] is a Feller process.
* [[Bessel process]]es are Feller processes.
* Solutions to [[stochastic differential equation]]s with [[Lipschitz continuous]] coefficients are Feller processes.{{citation needed|date=December 2015}}
* Every [[adapted process|adapted]] right continuous Feller process on a [[filtered probability space]] <math>(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, (\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\geq 0})</math> satisfies the [[strong Markov property]] with respect to the filtration <math>(\mathcal{F}_{t^+})_{t\geq 0}</math>, i.e., for each  <math>(\mathcal{F}_{t^+})_{t\geq 0}</math>-[[stopping time]]  <math>\tau</math>, conditioned on the event <math>\{\tau < \infty\}</math>, we have that for each <math>t\ge 0</math>, <math>X_{\tau + t}</math> is independent of <math>\mathcal{F}_{\tau^+}</math> given <math>X_\tau</math>.<ref>Rogers, L.C.G. and [[David Williams (mathematician)|Williams, David]]  ''Diffusions, Markov Processes and Martingales'' volume One: Foundations, second edition, John Wiley and Sons Ltd, 1979. (page 247, Theorem 8.3) </ref>
